text:
emma_support: Hi team -- customer JCorp reporting intermittent 502s from our hosted inference API when connecting via their PrivateLink. Happens after a config change on their side earlier today. Can we triage?

customer-jcorp: Hi! We flipped on a new egress allowlist for prod subnets and moved a few interface endpoints into a shared subnet. Since then our app gets fast failures to /v1/generate. Only visible via PrivateLink, internet traffic is fine.

kevin_sre: Can you share a curl output and a dig against the VPC endpoint DNS?

customer-jcorp: Sure. From an app pod inside the affected subnet:

customer-jcorp: ```
$ dig +short inference-api.prod.vpce.jcorp.internal
10.2.45.23

$ curl -v --resolve inference-api.prod.vpce.jcorp.internal:443:10.2.45.23 https://inference-api.prod.vpce.jcorp.internal/v1/generate\* Connected to inference-api.prod.vpce.jcorp.internal (10.2.45.23) port 443 (#0)\* TLS handshake error: Handshake failed\* Received HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway\{"error":"upstream read timeout"\}
```

diego_neteng: Ok TLS handshake error + 502 upstream read timeout suggests the connection to the backend (Redwood nodes) is failing after the VPCE/ENI accepts it. Two quick checks: 1) are the endpoint ENIs in the same AZ and routing table as the pods? 2) is their egress allowlist blocking outbound to our backend IPs or port 443?

emma_support: @customer-jcorp can you run a traceroute/tcpdump from the pod to 10.2.45.23 (the endpoint) and also show `ip route` and NAT gateway routes?

customer-jcorp: Pasting trimmed tcpdump:

customer-jcorp: ```
15:20:01.123 IP app-pod > 10.2.45.23: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
15:20:01.124 IP 10.2.45.23 > app-pod: Flags [S.], seq 1, ack 1, win 28960, options [mss 1460], length 0
15:20:01.130 IP app-pod > 10.2.45.23: Flags [P.], ack 1, length 512
15:20:01.131 IP 10.2.45.23 > app-pod: RST, length 0
```

diego_neteng: RST immediately after client data suggests either the ENI's SG or NACL is rejecting the response path or there's asymmetry (reply going out a NAT not expected). Do you use source/dest check on the ENI? If disabled on a router instance or TGW it can change flow.

customer-jcorp: We have a TGW in front of the subnets and source/dest is enabled on ENIs. We also have an egress allowlist enforced by firewall appliance that only permits outbound to a prefix-list of internal service IPs (they stabled last month).

kevin_sre: Can you `curl` the Redwood public domain (our fallback) from the same pod but forcing resolution to the Redwood private IP to see the direct TLS path? Example: `curl -v --resolve api.redwood-inference.com:443:10.10.78.90 https://api.redwood-inference.com/health`

customer-jcorp: Doing that now: it connects and completes TLS with 200 OK. So direct path to our backend IP in their routing works. The difference: when going through the PrivateLink endpoint, the IP is 10.2.45.23 (ENI).

emma_support: That indicates their firewall/egress is probably blocking outbound packets coming from the ENI IP range or the firewall is doing DNAT/inspection that breaks TLS SNI. Any TLS inspect/bump in the path?

customer-jcorp: The appliance does TLS inspection for outbound traffic to internet, but we exempted internal VPC ranges. However the egress allowlist also restricts destination IP ranges. We recently replaced the prefix-list for redwood from an AWS-managed list to a static CIDR block list.

diego_neteng: Hypothesis: Their allowlist contains our old backend CIDR, but PrivateLink resolves to private ENI IPs that are not in that prefix-list. The firewall then allows the SYN to the ENI but blocks ESTABLISHED/established traffic from the ENI back to the pod or resets connection. That explains the RST. Please share the prefix-list values and a `tcpdump -n` showing src/dst on RST packet.

customer-jcorp: Prefix-list entries: 10.10.78.0/24 (old), 52.9.0.0/16 (public fallbacks). The ENIs are 10.2.45.0/24.

infra-bot: Automated note: customer JCorp account shows VPCE interface endpoint in subnet subnet-0a2b3c with ENI 10.2.45.23 in us-west-2a. Traffic metrics show short-lived connections with RST spikes at 15:20 UTC.

kevin_sre: That matches. Two remediation paths: 1) add the ENI CIDR/prefix (10.2.45.0/24 or better, the VPCE subnet range) to their allowlist to permit stateful return traffic, OR 2) switch to Private Hosted Zone (PHZ) that routes to a stable private IP range they've already allowlisted, or 3) use our public endpoint with VPC egress allowed. We should validate SGs too: endpoint SG must allow 443 from the pod CIDR and outbound to backend nodes.

customer-jcorp: We updated the prefix-list to include 10.2.45.0/24 and redeployed the firewall policy. Retesting...

customer-jcorp: Test results: `curl` to the VPCE now succeeds with 200 and TLS handshake completes. No more RSTs in tcpdump.

emma_support: Great. Can you confirm whether the original root cause was the prefix-list not containing ENI CIDRs? Any secondary issues (PHZ overlap, route propagation) found?

customer-jcorp: Root cause: our egress allowlist referenced an outdated redwood CIDR and we had interface endpoints placed into a shared subnet not included in that prefix-list. Secondary note: because the VPCE ENIs were in a different AZ/subnet than some pods, reply paths hit the firewall appliance which enforced stateful rules and dropped the connection when return IP wasn't allowed. No PHZ conflicts found.

diego_neteng: Logging suggestion: add VPCE ENI CIDR ranges to monitoring for firewall hits and add an alert if VPCE TCP resets > 1% over 5m. Also, when customers move endpoints between subnets, they should re-evaluate prefix-lists and SGs.

kevin_sre: I'll mark this as resolved from our side. Action item for billing: none. @sara_billing FYI no billing impact, just connectivity policy change.

sara_billing: Thanks, noted.

emma_support: Closing the thread. Customer confirmed fix and will roll a small automation to sync endpoint subnet CIDRs into their allowlist. :thumbsup:

customer-jcorp: Thanks for the assist, team!
